crusadecraft.codex.name: CrusadeCraft Codex
crusadecraft.codex.subtitle: Ruling a realm
crusadecraft.codex.landing: Your MineColonies colonies become a realm: a council of real citizens, a treasury, laws, neighbours to win over or subdue, wars, intrigues and a court.$(br2)Each chapter explains one part of the game, in the order you discover it.
crusadecraft.codex.cat.guerre.desc: Casus belli, armies, sieges, peace, crusades.
crusadecraft.codex.fondation.p0: Place the $(l)Royal Throne$() in the Town Hall of a colony you own (level 2 or more), then right-click it: pick a name, a motto, a house and colours. The colony becomes your capital.
crusadecraft.codex.fondation.p1: The $(k:key.crusadecraft.realm_menu) key (K by default) opens the realm menu: realm, council, vassals, diplomacy, treasury, war, laws, chronicles. The $(l)Register$() shows your colonies; a button on the Town Hall window also opens the menu.
crusadecraft.codex.conseil.p0: Your councillors are real citizens. With the $(l)Sceptre$(), right-click a citizen: their sheet, traits, stats (from their MineColonies skills) and opinion of you. Appoint them chancellor, marshal, steward, spymaster or chaplain.
crusadecraft.codex.conseil.p1: The $(l)Council Table$() gathers the council; each member gets a task (manage the demesne, train troops, hunt plots…). Mayors run each province from their $(l)Desk$(). The discontent bring requests, or band together.
crusadecraft.codex.tresor.p0: Every world day, colonies pay taxes according to their buildings and happiness; demesne income, wages and upkeep follow. The $(l)Treasury Chest$() takes and gives gold (nuggets, ingots, blocks).
crusadecraft.codex.tresor.p1: Laws (taxation, authority, chivalry, justice) are voted by the council, or forced through at a prestige cost. Some need University research.
crusadecraft.codex.carte.p0: AI realms live around you, set on real villages: you discover them by travelling, or by receiving their heralds. Nine $(l)War Table$() frames make a map; the "Map" button opens the world map, political or de jure.
crusadecraft.codex.diplomatie.p0: At the $(l)Dovecote$(), write to other rulers: treaties, gifts, insults, tributes, vassalage. Their answer can be read in advance, and comes by letter. An accepted letter is sealed with the $(l)Royal Seal$().
crusadecraft.codex.diplomatie.p1: The $(l)Chancery Table$() creates your titles (County, Duchy, Kingdom, Empire) once you have enough provinces, sets your vassals' contracts and has your chancellor fabricate claims.
crusadecraft.codex.guerre.p0: At the War Table, pick a realm and a casus belli: claim, de jure right, conquest, subjugation, humiliation. Your allies and vassals follow. Raise the army: it counts in full but costs pay.
crusadecraft.codex.guerre.p1: Each day, a skirmish. Approach the enemy capital: its garrison sallies out; hold its banner to take the place. The enemy raids your colonies. In enemy territory, only explosives break blocks, and everything is repaired at peace.
crusadecraft.codex.guerre.p2: Peace is negotiated at the Table: white peace, demand victory, surrender. Victory gives the target province, a vassal or gold. Mind your $(l)threat$(): too many conquests, and a coalition forms against you.
crusadecraft.codex.croisades.p0: Some realms are pagan or heretic. As at least a count, with 100 piety, declare a $(l)holy war$() on them: faithful realms rally, other rulers are called. Victory: the target province, and piety and prestige for every crusader.
crusadecraft.codex.evenements.p0: Famine, fever, feasts, pilgrims, brigands… An event awaits your decision for a few days ("Events" button of the realm menu); without an answer, the default option applies. Events are JSON files: a datapack can add more.
crusadecraft.codex.complots.p0: Discontent courtiers band into factions (lower taxes, independence, dismissal of a councillor) and issue ultimatums. Those who hate you plot. Your spymaster uncovers them, along with secrets good for blackmail.
crusadecraft.codex.complots.p1: All of this is shown in the $(l)Intrigues$() screen (Council tab). Dread, a marshal keeping order and a named heir weaken factions. Unhappy, overtaxed colonies revolt.
crusadecraft.codex.chroniques.p0: The chronicle of your reign writes itself: founding, titles, wars, conquests, laws, decisions. Read it in the Chronicles tab, along with world news, or in the $(l)Chronicles of the Realm$() book.
crusadecraft.codex.tournois.p0: Place $(l)Tournament Lists$() in your realm ("Chivalry" research). Your councillors and mayors joust against neighbouring champions: prestige for the host, a champion trait for the winner, sometimes wounds.
crusadecraft.codex.maison.p0: From the Realm tab, "House" button: bring citizens into your dynasty. Their spouses and children (the real MineColonies genealogy) follow. Name an heir to reassure the court.
crusadecraft.codex.maison.p1: Marry a free member into the family of an AI ruler of your faith: the answer can be read in advance, the letter is sealed, and both houses become allies.
